name: Matplotlib
summary: Matplotlib is the foundational Python plotting library for producing static, animated, and interactive figures. Its design is centered on a low-level figure/axes/artist hierarchy, which gives engineers fine-grained control over every visual element. It is best understood as a low-level, highly configurable rendering system rather than a declarative charting layer, commonly used when publication-quality output and exact canvas control are required.

tasks.avoid_when: 1) You need immediate redraw completion. 2) Batch scripts. 3) Non-interactive backends. 4) You are not using event-driven updates. 5) A direct `draw` is sufficient.
tasks.decision_notes:
Category: Output
Module: `pyplot`
Return Value: `None`.
Expected Output: A redraw is queued for the active GUI loop.
Performance Notes: Better than repeated immediate redraws in event-driven UIs.
Common Mistakes: Expecting immediate visual completion; using it in headless code; calling it without an interactive loop; replacing explicit redraw logic blindly; ignoring backend behavior.
Related APIs: `draw`, `pause`, `ion`.
gotchas: Idle redraws depend on the event loop
it is designed for efficiency, not determinism

package_specific_debugging: Warning: 'UserWarning: Starting a Matplotlib GUI outside the main thread' occurs when using interactive backends in non-main threads. Switch backend to Agg: `import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')` before importing pyplot.
Memory leak in loops: Call `plt.close(fig)` or `fig.clear()` after `savefig()` inside loops to free memory.
Overlapping labels or text: Use `fig.tight_layout()` or `constrained_layout=True` to automatically calculate margins.
migration_notes: Matplotlib 3.8+ deprecated several older colormaps and styling conventions.
Use `seaborn-v0_8` instead of deprecated `seaborn` styles in style sheets.
breaking_changes: Starting with version 3.0+, several pyplot stateful functions return different types or are discouraged in class-based architectures.
